Someone sent you a number.

Probably your CTO, with a date next to it. This page explains what it means and what you can do with it. It takes two minutes.

Example resultAT RISK
34%chance of shipping 67 items by March 15. About 1 in 3.
RealisticMay 24, 2027
Gap10 weeks late

Yours will have your project, your date and your number.

What it is

A forecast, built from how fast your team actually finished work in the last twelve weeks. A computer played the remaining work forward 10,000 times. The percentage is how often it was done by the date. The realistic date is the one that 85 of 100 runs made. Both are the best case: they assume no work is added and the team keeps its recent pace.

It is not an estimate, not an opinion and not a performance review.

Read it like a weather forecast. A 30% chance of rain isn't wrong on a dry day.

What a low number means

A low number rarely means a slow team. It usually means the date was fixed before anyone could know, or the work grew after the date was set.

The person who sent it didn't cause it. They measured it.

What you can change

Time

Move the date to the realistic one, and tell the client now instead of later.

Scope

Keep the date and ship less by then. The card says how much less.

Pace

Remove what slows the team down. Adding people rarely works in time.

Questions to ask back

  1. Which would you change?
  2. What is stuck right now, and what would unstick it?
  3. How do our other dates look?

The number doesn't say why.

It says whether the date will be made. Why not, and what to change, is the next question. The Delivery Audit answers it in writing, and its first page is written for you.
